property_summary: For every admissible call to transfer(...) the reference contract C always returns true (call succeeds and returns true); the mutant changes the final return to false so some inputs produce a successful call that returns false, violating this rule.
For every admissible input where transfer(...) completes (does not revert), the reference C returns true; the mutant that returns false will therefore cause a differing return value for some inputs.

For any admissible inputs that make transfer(...) complete (not revert), the reference C returns true; the mutant that returns false will cause some completing calls to return false, so asserting that transfer(...) returns true distinguishes the mutant.

For any admissible inputs where transfer(...) completes (does not revert), the reference contract C always returns true; the mutant that returns false will for some completing inputs make transfer(...) return false, violating this rule.

For every admissible input where transfer(...) completes (does not revert), the reference contract C returns true; the mutant that returns false will for some inputs make transfer(...) complete but return false, so the property asserts that transfer(...) returns true for all admissible inputs.
Only the owner address can successfully invoke transfer; for any caller other than owner the transfer call must revert (i.e. not return true).
Calling transfer from any address other than the owner's address always reverts (i.e., reverted == true) for all non-empty _tos arrays.
If the caller is not the specific owner address then calling transfer with a non-empty _tos array always reverts.
Only the owner can call transfer successfully: for any caller address not equal to the stored owner, calling transfer with a non-empty _tos array always reverts (i.e., reverted == true).
For any caller other than the stored owner address, calling transfer with a non-empty _tos array always reverts (i.e., reverted == true).
